meta.coords: All boxes are [x0,y0,x1,y1] in source pixels of `path` (w x h). One box per text line of the phrase, 3 px padding, from tesseract word boxes (psm 3 and 6, plus an inverted pass for dark images; images narrower than 1000 px were OCR-upscaled 2-3x and the boxes mapped back).
meta.quality: 1-5, legibility when the image is shown 700-900 px wide on a phone: median OCR line height of the highlighted phrase at 800 px display width: >=50 px = 5, >=36 = 4, >=26 = 3, >=17 = 2, else 1; minus 1 if the source needs more than 1.6x upscaling to reach 800 px, minus 1 if OCR confirms less than 75% of the text. 5 = big display type, 4 = comfortable, 3 = legible, 2 = barely legible (crop/zoom advised), 1 = unreadable.
meta.ocr_check: score = how much of `text` (first 300 chars) the OCR confirms (1.0 = all). note = real differences between the verified text and the OCR (single-letter noise such as I/l is ignored); highlight_scores = OCR match score per highlight phrase; line_px_at_800 = median highlight line height at 800 px width.
meta.lyric: keys of research/long/lyrics/*.json the screenshot fits (best first); tags are topic tags.
meta.source: deck-images.json (William deck) + assets/research/*/manifest.json (verified headline text, outlet, date, url); images are real screenshots, never re-typeset.

There is an extensive and ongoing review related to our agents’ use of internet access during training and evaluation. We’ve been publishing summaries at the link below and will continue to.
